questions: What existing infrastructure can support an approval-gated execute mode across the Helix + NetSuite stack?
Can a NetSuite beforeSubmit UserEventScript reliably make external HTTP calls to Helix mainland within governance limits?
What competing approaches exist for dry-run/approval/execution and what are their trade-offs?
What data model changes are needed to track approval state?
Which repositories need changes and what is the scope per repo?
How can proposed record changes be presented to non-technical NetSuite admins for meaningful approval?

answers.answer: Zero approval infrastructure exists. The building blocks are: (1) EXECUTE enum in TicketMode (Prisma + client types) with no specialized behavior, (2) ns-gm RESTlet executing arbitrary SuiteScript via new Function() with 24 N/* modules (fire-and-forget, no intercept), (3) NsDeployment model providing a pattern for async operations with status tracking (SDF file deploys only), (4) NS-GM credentials stored per org per environment (SANDBOX/PRODUCTION), (5) Workflow step chain treating EXECUTE identically to AUTO. No approval models, API routes, UI components, beforeSubmit scripts, or NS-to-Helix callback channels exist.

answers.answer: A beforeSubmit UserEventScript CAN make N/https calls, but governance constraints are significant. User Event Scripts have ~1000 usage units per execution. N/https.post costs approximately 10 units per call. However, there are compounding concerns: (1) Governance chaining — when RESTlet-executed code triggers a record.submit() which fires a beforeSubmit UES, governance costs compound across script contexts. (2) HTTP latency — external calls add wall-clock time which may cause timeouts. (3) Best practice guidance says to keep beforeSubmit lean (validation only) and push heavy operations to afterSubmit. The approach IS technically feasible but adds fragility and governance risk.

answers.answer: Six approaches identified for analysis in the research phase: (A) BeforeSubmit intercept with Helix mainland approval check (ticket owner's proposal), (B) Two-phase RESTlet with dry-run action (read-only preview then approved execute), (C) Pre-execution state snapshot via read-only script analysis, (D) Sandbox-first execution with production replay after approval, (E) Suitelet-based approval UI within NetSuite, (F) Server-side script simulation with change prediction. Each has distinct trade-offs in accuracy, governance cost, UX complexity, and implementation scope. The recommended approach for deeper evaluation is (B) Two-phase RESTlet — it avoids beforeSubmit governance chaining, keeps change capture deterministic, requires no new NetSuite script deployment, and reuses the existing ns-gm execution pathway.

answers.answer: New Prisma models needed: (1) NsExecuteRequest — tracks the full lifecycle of an execute request (proposed, dry-running, pending-approval, approved, executing, succeeded, failed), linking to ticket, organization, and user. (2) NsExecuteApproval — records human approval/rejection with before/after state snapshots, approving user, and timestamp. (3) NsExecuteScript — stores the proposed script string, its parameters, and the deterministic execution context. These follow the existing NsDeployment/NsDeploymentTicket pattern for async operations with status tracking.

answers.answer: All three primary repos need changes; helix-cli is context-only. (1) helix-global-server: New Prisma models for approval state, new API endpoints for approval CRUD/status, workflow step modifications for EXECUTE mode, deterministic script executor service. (2) helix-global-client: Approval review UI, before/after diff visualization, approval action components (approve/reject), pending approval indicators, execute mode-specific ticket detail views. (3) ns-gm: RESTlet extension with 'dry-run' action for change preview capture, possibly 'execute-approved' action with token validation. (4) helix-cli: No immediate changes needed; approval management is better handled through the Helix web UI.

answers.answer: The approval UX must translate SuiteScript operations into human-readable record change summaries. The two-phase RESTlet approach enables this: the dry-run phase captures the before-state (via record.load) and the proposed after-state (field values the script would set) without committing. The server can then generate a diff showing 'Customer: Acme Corp, Field: creditLimit, Before: 50000, After: 75000' in a structured format the client renders as a side-by-side or inline diff. The existing deployment-detail.tsx pattern (status tracking with step progression) and ns-setup-wizard-dialog.tsx (multi-step flow) provide UI patterns to follow.

statement: This is a greenfield research ticket requiring architectural design of an approval-gated execute mode for Helix NetSuite. Zero approval infrastructure exists across all four repositories. The EXECUTE enum value exists but has no specialized behavior. The core design challenge is creating a dry-run/approval/execution cycle that navigates NetSuite governance constraints while providing a frictionless UX for non-technical admins. The ticket owner proposed a beforeSubmit UserEventScript approach; five additional competing approaches should be evaluated. The recommended approach for detailed research is a two-phase RESTlet extension (dry-run + execute-approved actions) combined with server-side approval state management and client-side diff-based approval UI. This avoids beforeSubmit governance chaining risks and leverages the existing ns-gm execution pathway.
